positions.why: UNH beat Q2 EPS by about 30% and raised FY26 guidance a second time, to $19.50–20.00, but the stock rose only 1.2% on the news; that under-reaction in a low-volatility name (2.7% weekly) with no report this week is a textbook post-earnings drift setup.
PLD's beat, second guidance raise and record leasing drove XLRE's new 52-week high; the move is backed by earnings rather than hopes of rate cuts, and PLD has no report this week.
SPG is the Council's main single-stock setup: the cheapest REIT at 15.4x with a 3.98% yield, near its highs alongside KIM, REG and FRT; hold above $225 into the Jul 28 report, stop at $215.

MSFT rose 2.3% in tech's worst week of 2026, trades at 23.5x trailing earnings with about 40% upside to the mean target, and doesn't report until Jul 29, which keeps the book tied to SPY's biggest weights.
BAC is the rate beneficiary from Wire #1: the yield curve is steepening, it made a new 52-week high after earnings at 15x, and financials' low correlation to SPY (0.16) offsets the REITs' rate risk.

thesis: Tech's worst week of 2026 was money moving between sectors, not money leaving the market: 8 of 11 sectors rose as funds left high-priced AI hardware for companies with real cash flow and raised guidance, and the Fed meeting plus the MSFT/META/AAPL/AMZN reports come the week after. This week is full of all-or-nothing earnings reports (TSLA, GOOGL, INTC, UNP, TMO, FCX/NEM, SLB, the telecoms), and the Council's lesson this season is that only guidance moves stocks and options underprice the moves. So the book owns names that have already reported and beaten (UNH, PLD, BAC) or report after the window (SPG, MSFT), and holds nothing that reports Jul 20–24. It also skips the energy rally driven by the war and the refiners that already look exhausted (up over 20% in four weeks), as all three agents agreed. MSFT keeps some exposure to the rebound case for tech after its valuation reset, BAC offsets the REITs' sensitivity to rates, and 20% cash covers the oil-to-Fed-to-valuations risk after the VIX jumped on Friday.
risks: A US–Iran escalation that pushes WTI above $90 and the 10Y toward 4.75% would hit PLD, SPG and MSFT together, while a ceasefire or a sharp chip rebound would leave this cautious, lower-beta book behind SPY; managed-care contagion (ELV fell 10% last week) could cap UNH. I have no memory of how this week actually went and used only the folder, some of which is stale or contradictory (earnings dates, the semis wiki's prices).
